procedure: Take a magnetic compass. Put it on a table and see which end of its needle points north. The N-pole of the needle is usually coloured red.
Place a bar magnet on the table. Bring the compass near to its N-pole. Observe the direction in which the N-pole of the needle stays.
Put the compass near to the S-pole of the bar magnet. Observe the direction in which the N-pole of the needle stays this time.
Place the head of an iron nail in contact with the S-pole of the bar magnet.

Put the compass near to the pointed end of the iron nail. Observe the direction in which the N-pole of the needle settles. Note whether the nail has become a magnet and whether magnetism has been induced in it.
Take the bar magnet away from the nail. Again check the behaviour of the nail by bringing the compass near to its ends. Observe whether the magnetism vanishes.
aim: To observe the direction of a compass needle near a bar magnet and demonstrate induced magnetism in an iron nail.

viva.question: Which end of a compass needle points north?
What happens to the compass N-pole near the bar magnet’s N-pole?
viva.answer: It points away from the magnet’s N-pole.

viva.question: What happens to the compass N-pole near the bar magnet’s S-pole?
viva.answer: It points towards the magnet’s S-pole.

viva.question: Which pole is induced at the nail’s head when it touches the magnet’s S-pole?
viva.answer: An N-pole is induced at the nail’s head.

viva.question: Which pole is induced at the nail’s pointed end?
viva.answer: An S-pole is induced at the pointed end.

viva.question: What happens to the nail’s induced magnetism when the bar magnet is removed?

rows: Near nail’s pointed end while its head touches the magnet’s S-pole
Pointed end acts as an S-pole
Near the nail after removing the bar magnet
No clear attraction to either end

diagram: Draw two labelled sketches: a bar magnet with N and S poles and a compass near each pole, showing the compass N-pole pointing away from N and towards S; then draw the magnet’s S-pole touching the nail’s head, label the nail end at the head N and its pointed end S, and show a nearby compass with its N-pole pointing towards the nail’s pointed end.
title: Induced magnetism in an iron nail
precautions: Keep the compass on a level table and allow its needle to settle before observing.
Keep the compass close to the magnet or nail, but do not let it touch them.
Ensure that the nail’s head remains in contact with the magnet’s S-pole during the observation.
Keep other magnets and magnetic objects away from the compass during the activity.
result: The S-pole of the bar magnet induces an N-pole at the nail’s head and an S-pole at its pointed end. The nail’s induced magnetism vanishes when the bar magnet is removed.
